Scenarios: car speeds and traffic stress

Source: vignettes/articles/scenarios.Rmd
scenarios.Rmd

Every routing function takes three arguments that change the street network for that call only: new_carspeeds (car speeds by ‘OpenStreetMap’ way, or by area), carspeed_scale (a factor for every other street) and new_lts (levels of traffic stress for cyclists, by way or by line). The network itself does not change. This page uses the Porto Alegre sample of r5r 2.5.0 and the scenario tables that come with it.

library(peabiru)
poa <- poa_sample(c("poa_osm.pbf", "poa_hexgrid.csv", "poa_osm_congestion.csv",
                    "poa_poly_congestion.rds", "poa_osm_lts.csv", "poa_ls_lts.rds"))
poa_network <- build_network(poa, n_threads = 2)
hexes <- read.csv(file.path(poa, "poa_hexgrid.csv"))
pts <- hexes[seq(1, nrow(hexes), by = 25), ]

car <- function(...) {
  travel_time_matrix(poa_network, pts, pts, mode = "CAR", n_threads = 2, ...)
}
base <- car()
mean(base$travel_time_p50)
#> [1] 13.9768

Car speeds by way

A data frame with osm_id, max_speed and speed_type gives, for each way, a factor of its car speed ("scale") or a new speed ("km/h"); a speed of 0 closes the way to cars.

congestion <- read.csv(file.path(poa, "poa_osm_congestion.csv"))
head(congestion)
#>      osm_id max_speed speed_type
#> 1  27184648       0.5      scale
#> 2 762361901       0.5      scale
#> 3 568609955       0.5      scale
#> 4 709834913       0.5      scale
#> 5 709834914       0.5      scale
#> 6  77705540       0.5      scale
slow <- car(new_carspeeds = congestion)
mean(slow$travel_time_p50)
#> [1] 13.9836

carspeed_scale multiplies the car speed of every street the table leaves out (all of them without a table):

rush_hour <- car(carspeed_scale = 0.7)
mean(rush_hour$travel_time_p50)
#> [1] 18.2156

Car speeds are kept as 16-bit centimetres per second, so a factor or a speed that would bring a speed to 0 or less, or beyond that range, is an error rather than a wrapped-around speed.

Car speeds by area

An sf data frame of polygons with poly_id, scale and priority gives each street the factor of the polygon it meets with the highest priority (ties: the one it overlaps most).

areas <- readRDS(file.path(poa, "poa_poly_congestion.rds"))
areas
#> Simple feature collection with 2 features and 3 fields
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: -51.24537 ymin: -30.04352 xmax: -51.21426 ymax: -30.02548
#> Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84
#>   poly_id scale priority                       geometry
#> 1       1   0.7        1 POLYGON ((-51.22463 -30.034...
#> 2       2   0.8        2 POLYGON ((-51.21426 -30.034...
by_area <- car(new_carspeeds = areas)
mean(by_area$travel_time_p50)
#> [1] 14.0304

Traffic stress

new_lts changes the level of traffic stress (1 to 4) cyclists meet, by way (osm_id, lts) or along lines (an sf of LINESTRINGs with line_id, lts and priority, each street taking the level of the nearest line). A cyclist rides only on streets up to max_lts and walks the bicycle elsewhere:

lts <- read.csv(file.path(poa, "poa_osm_lts.csv"))
head(lts)
#>      osm_id lts
#> 1  27184648   1
#> 2 762361901   1
#> 3 568609955   1
#> 4 709834913   1
#> 5 709834914   1
#> 6  77705540   1
bike <- function(...) {
  travel_time_matrix(poa_network, pts, pts, mode = "BICYCLE", max_lts = 2,
                     n_threads = 2, ...)
}
c(base = mean(bike()$travel_time_p50),
  scenario = mean(bike(new_lts = lts)$travel_time_p50))
#>     base scenario 
#> 51.53024 51.48387

A scenario changes the street search from the origins (the trip without public transport, and access to it by bicycle or car) but not the egress from the stops, and, on a network with an elevation raster, the call runs without slope costs, with a warning (see Elevation).
